character_facts: The three whore-priestesses travel together as a group.
At least one of the priestesses is calculating and manipulative, using the threat of the vessel as a message to eavesdroppers.
The older priestess appears physically withered or corpse-like but remains active and authoritative.
The group is concerned about possible treachery and about the Metabaron learning their intentions.
characters_present: An older, heavily decayed or skeletal-looking priestess among the trio
Small robotic attendants or transport robots
The transporter or its catayborg controller (mentioned, not clearly personified on-page)
continuity_links: This page transitions the three whore-priestesses into transport aboard a robo-transporter.
It sets up a timed window created by sedating the transporter's catayborg.
It foreshadows confrontation involving Okhar and the Metabaron through the threat conveyed over the transporter's surveillance.
dialogue_meaning: The priestesses invoke Jejoh for help and blessing.
A narration box identifies the arriving craft as a Harana-class robo-transporter sent to collect them.
One of the travelers explains that the transporter or its controller has been sedated with pentalina for two hours.
They intend to return before the sedation ends; otherwise the vessel will turn violent.
They deliberately mention the vessel's destructive power in case the transporter is being monitored, so the Metabaron will be warned against betrayal or interference.
locations: Inside a Harana-class robo-transporter cockpit or passenger compartment
Near or alongside a larger ship or structure
lore_facts: A vehicle type called a Harana-class robo-transporter exists in this setting.
There are three figures identified as whore-priestesses.
A substance called pentalina can be used to incapacitate a catayborg for a limited time.
A catayborg is associated with controlling or operating the transporter.
The transport vessel is described as an organic vessel.
If reactivated under the stated conditions, the vessel is said capable of reducing a planet or region to rubble.
Jejoh the Pure is a revered figure invoked in prayer or blessing.
plot_events: A Harana-class robo-transporter arrives to collect three whore-priestesses.
The trio travels aboard the transporter through space near a planet.
One speaker says the transporter or its catayborg controller was drugged with pentalina and will remain inactive for about two hours.
The speakers discuss a contingency: if they do not return in time, the craft will attack and cause massive destruction.
One priestess approves speaking openly about the vessel's power so that any hidden listeners will carry the warning to the Metabaron.
uncertainties: Several proper names are hard to read precisely from the image, including 'Jejoh,' 'Harana,' 'pentalina,' 'catayborg,' and 'Okhar.'
It is not fully clear whether the sedated target is the transporter itself, an onboard controller, or another associated being.
The exact larger structure or ship seen outside the transporter is not identified on this page alone.
visual_summary: Three hooded priestess-like figures ride inside a spacecraft cockpit, framed in close-up with mechanical controls and attendants around them. Exterior panels show a transport craft approaching or docked with a larger vessel in space above a planet. In the final panel, an older, withered member of the trio speaks while small robotic figures are visible in the background inside the craft.
